abstract: If benign cystic teratomas (dermoid cysts) of the ovary arise from a germ cell that has undergone meiosis, they should be missing genes which are present in the person. Three independently segregating allelic isozymes in 11 benign cystic teratomas of the human female ovary were compared with normal tissue of the same case. Dermoid cysts from persons heterozygous for these isozymes are frequently homozygous for that particular gene product. One of two dermoid cysts is homozygous for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase, two of four tumors are homozygous for phosphoglucomutase at the PGM(1) locus, and two (or more) of eight tumors are homozygous for phosphoglucomutase at the PGM(3) locus in women heterozygous for these allelic isozymes. These findings are consistent with the hypothesis that these tumors arise from a germ cell which has undergone meiosis with varying degrees of crossing-over.
abstract_ja: 良性嚢胞性奇形腫（類皮嚢腫）が減数分裂を経た胚細胞に由来するならば、本来個体が持つ遺伝子の一部を欠くはずである。ヒトの卵巣に生じた良性嚢胞性奇形腫11例について、独立に分離する3種の対立アイソザイムを、同一症例の正常組織と比較した。これらのアイソザイムについてヘテロ接合性の女性に生じた類皮嚢腫は、しばしば特定の遺伝子産物についてホモ接合性を示した。すなわち、グルコース-6-リン酸デヒドロゲナーゼについては2例中1例、ホスホグルコムターゼのPGM(1)座については4例中2例、PGM(3)座については8例中2例以上がホモ接合性であった。これらの所見は、これらの腫瘍が種々の程度の交叉を伴う減数分裂を経た胚細胞に由来するという仮説と一致する。
